title: robot_models: five Model-first APIs
brief: Make Model the base object and let each type organize its models into a ladder, so that with a datasheet and a rig log in hand the next steps (build, predict, fit, compare rungs) read naturally.
defaultWhy: Subclass ladder is the AI recommendation at 88.5/100, first for both judges (user lens 91, maintainer lens 86). It is the most literal reading of 'Model as the base object': each rung is a typed frozen dataclass whose fields are its parameters and whose MRO is its fallback, and it fits, predicts on arrays, scores held-out data and exports MuJoCo attributes itself. Its price is upkeep: until the classes become the source, every rung is written twice (class + Rung record), a new rung needs a class, a record, the rung folder and a seeds() override (fr5 = 2 from both judges), and a Rung added without a class silently drops out of its ladder. Closest alternative: Estimators that climb at 83.0, where one call, servo.climb(datasheet, fit, test), answers 'what now' as an additive layer over v1.
decisionHinge: The lead rests on fr1 (the Model you hold) against fr4/fr5 (migration, cost of a new rung). Moving about 10 points from fr1 to fr4 lets Records in a Family tie Estimators that climb for first (its Family subclasses today's Ladder; sim2real's parity test passed 56 with Families in place of Ladders). Reading 'what now' as 'tell me which rig motion to run next' lifts Type kit level with Estimators that climb. Neither flip overtakes Subclass ladder unless migration or rung cost is weighted up. The contested assumption is judging it on its end state (the class tree replaces ladder.py's records, a ruler edit) rather than on the interim duplicate.
invariants: The integrated_servo ladder's 14 keys in today's order, and its fallback chains.
One vocabulary per type; frictionloss_nm resolves to coulomb_friction.
The physics in actuators/rungs/*/model.py is reused, not retyped.
One shared scenario: an illustrative servo datasheet and a simulated rig log from a hidden truth.
boundary: Each variant is a runnable prototype in docs/proposals/api-2026-11-17/ that passes the frozen check: fits recover the hidden truth, and the rung is chosen on held-out plateaus, with a negative control where the simpler rung must win. Runnable physics M0–M3 only; nothing in src/, the ruler, robotparts or sim2real changed.

variants.name: Subclass ladder
variants.thesis: A Model is a frozen dataclass whose fields are its parameters, and a rung subclasses the rung it extends. The type's ladder is its class tree and the fallback is its MRO. The held-out choice walks that MRO upward and takes the first fitted instance whose held-out rms is within 1.5× the rig's noise floor.
variants.bestWhen: Rungs really are refinements that nest their base (friction does), contributors write Python, and values flow into code as typed attributes that pyright checks (still 0 errors at pyright 1.1.390). Nesting is also what makes the held-out choice well posed: a subclass that reduces to its base is exactly where training error cannot choose and held-out error can. Inheritance gives the order for free, so the rule needs no separate ladder ranking.
variants.losesWhen: This loses in four cases. First, a choice between siblings (Stribeck or Load at M3): compare() orders only one chain, so it takes two comparisons against M2, and a tie between two siblings that both reach the floor is left to the user. Second, a rung that combines siblings (multiple inheritance gives a C3 fallback you may not mean). Third, non-Python consumers (robotparts JS/JSON, sim2real cards) cannot see a class. Fourth, "optional below, needed above" fields conflict with pyright for hand-declared M1 fields. Smaller costs: parameters share a namespace with the API, and a rung's fields are spread across 4-9 class bodies. The fit is unbounded: on servo B the overfit M3 lands at stribeck_velocity = -1.16.

decisions.label: Rule
decisions.value: This is sim2real's select(): the lowest rung whose held-out rms ÷ noise floor is at most 1.5 (SELECT_LIMIT, copied from TWINNED_LIMIT). It replaces v0's training-log BIC: the held-out test is the direct parsimony question, the bar is in the rig's own units, the rule matches sim2real's choice, and it can return None when no rung is good enough.

decisions.label: Order = MRO
decisions.value: compare() sorts models by MRO length and refuses a set that is not one inheritance chain, checked with isinstance(upper, type(lower)). The class tree itself defines "lowest rung", and comparing siblings (Stribeck vs Load) raises TypeError.

decisions.label: Where it lives
decisions.value: score(log) is an instance method on Model and compare() is a classmethod on the type root. noise_floor(log) is a module function because it belongs to the log, not to any model. Comparison.chosen applies the rule, and fitted_on= only adds a fit-rms column for contrast.

decisions.label: Fit only on fit split
decisions.value: Scenario step 4 fits on rig_log(case, "fit"), and steps 5-6 compare on rig_log(case, "test"). run(case) substitutes the case into a "<case>" placeholder in steps 1-5 and never branches on it. Step 6 (servo B) is a literal transcript-only repeat of the same calls.

keepParts: Order the held-out choice by the fallback chain itself: sort candidates by fallback length and refuse a set that is not one chain (isinstance(upper, type(lower))). Any variant can do this with its own fallback().

A Comparison table that shows fit rms beside held-out rms and ÷ floor, in mN·m, with chosen = None when no rung reaches 1.5× floor ('climb a rung, or measure more'). It makes the overfit visible: on case B, M3 is 3.97 vs 4.04 on fit and 6.62 vs 4.33 held out.
Typed rung classes via PEP 681 dataclass_transform with __init_subclass__ registration and an import-time guard against v1's rung records (the ladder is found by declaration, so no registry).

media.caption: What changes for the ruler, robotparts' vendoring and sim2real's parity test.
media.html: The plan is unchanged by the amendment and stays additive. score, compare and noise_floor are new API and touch no v1 record. Now: the classes sit beside v1's records and are checked against them at import, so tests/test_ladders_acceptance.py, the actuators/rungs/* bytes (robotparts' tools/sync_actuator_rungs.py and tests/core/test_actuator_rungs_vendored.py) and sim2real's tests/test_robot_models_parity.py (which reads ladders() live via holds/rung/fallback) are all untouched. The ruler needs edits only for what the classes don't hold yet (vocabulary, aliases, packed, deployment-only, wears, composes), landed first and alone. Selection parity: sim2real's parity rule 2 already checks that each card rung's base is in the mapped rung's fallback(), which here is the MRO that compare() walks. The 1.5 limit is copied, not imported (robot_models never reads sim2real), so add one assertion SELECT_LIMIT == TWINNED_LIMIT to sim2real's parity test when this lands.

variants.name: Records in a Family
variants.thesis: A Model is a frozen record (key, level, base, parameters with units, equation, references) that carries its attached physics and binds to separately held values to become a callable, lmfit-style fittable BoundModel; a Family, literally a subclass of v1's Ladder, holds the type's vocabulary, aliases and model tree, and because only it knows the tree, it also judges it: family.compare(...) scores fitted models on held-out data and picks the lowest rung within 1.5x the rig's noise floor.
variants.bestWhen: Landing without breaking anyone matters most: the Family IS a v1 Ladder, so ladders() could hand out Families with no consumer edit. Also good when rungs keep arriving as robotparts-style model.py + model.json folders: binding, fitting and the held-out comparison against the floor all come free. And when the rung chosen in robot_models should be the same one sim2real twins, because both use the same select() rule and limit.
variants.losesWhen: The Model should stand alone. It can describe and compute itself, but fallback, siblings and choosing a rung all need its Family, and parameters are names in a dict that type checkers cannot see. The fitter has no physical bounds: on case B, M3 fits breakaway -4.73 N·m at 0.0107 rad/s. The held-out choice discards that fit, but nothing flags it on the BoundModel. Stateful (LuGre dt) or jointly nonlinear physics needs more than the linear/nonlinear probe. FLOOR_LIMIT duplicates sim2real's TWINNED_LIMIT, because robot_models cannot import sim2real.

decisions.label: Where the held-out comparison lives
decisions.value: On the Family: family.compare(*bound, observed=, repeats=, **inputs). 'Lowest rung' is the tree's order, which only the Family knows; rows sort by depth (len(family.fallback(key))), and same-depth siblings sort best first.

decisions.label: Selection rule
decisions.value: sim2real's select(): the lowest rung whose held-out rms / noise floor <= 1.5 (FLOOR_LIMIT, the same value as sim2real's TWINNED_LIMIT; limit= can override it). Checked against the alternatives on the data: training rms fails case B (a mutated scratch copy gives FAIL). Training BIC happens to pick M2 (delta 4.0) but is graded on data the fit saw. Lowest held-out rms picks M2 by only 1.03 vs 1.04. The floor rule gives an absolute stop and does not depend on that 1% gap.

decisions.label: Noise floor is data, not model state
decisions.value: noise_floor(observed, repeats) is the pooled within-repeat std; compare takes repeats=log['plateau'] alongside observed. In the PyBaMM spirit, values and data stay apart from the record, and nothing about the rig is stored on a Model.

decisions.label: BIC removed
decisions.value: v0's training-data BIC column and rule are gone. The Comparison shows fit rms beside held-out rms and the ratio to the floor, so a reader can see a rung that trains better and tests worse.

keepParts: Family.compare ordering rows by depth in the tree (len(fallback(key))) and reading sim2real's floor rule, returning a Comparison whose .best is the chosen BoundModel ready to hand on (.mujoco(), callable on numpy)

noise_floor(observed, repeats) plus the fit-rms | held-out-rms | / floor table: the floor comes from the log's own repeats, and overfitting is visible at a glance (case B: M3 trains better, tests worse)

variants.name: Composed terms
variants.thesis: A Model is a sum of small term models, one per slot (inertia, friction, ripple, drivetrain, electrics, wear, correction), with parameters that are the union of the terms' parameters. A ladder key such as M3.stribeck is a named preset of slot choices. Climbing means swapping or filling one slot, and a swap pays only when the rung below it misses the rig's noise floor on plateaus neither fit saw.
variants.bestWhen: Effects are orthogonal and you want combinations no rung names (stribeck + ripple, dcmotor on load friction) through + or redeclare, with no new rung. It also suits a ladder that is mostly 'fill the next slot', and a reviewer who wants each climb shown as one named slot swap. The held-out table makes 'this swap paid (20.28 → 1.00)' or 'did not pay (1.03 → 1.57)' a single row labelled with the slot it changed.
variants.losesWhen: It loses when effects inside one slot interact: stribeck AND load-dependent friction cannot be written as stribeck + load, so it needs a combined option or nested slots. It also loses when one rung spans slots (v1's drivetrain repeats ripple's harmonics), and when the fallback is not 'undo the last slot change'. The held-out rule needs a log with repeated plateaus (plateau ids) to read the floor from. Without them this compare cannot judge until the floor is stated some other way. The core is 347 lines, against a 250-line target.

decisions.label: Where the held-out choice lives
decisions.value: On the comparison of Bounds, not on the Model or Slots: compare(*fits, on=test_log). A climb is one slot swap, so each row of the Comparison is one swap plus its held-out rms ÷ floor. 'This swap did not pay' (case B) is a row, not a separate report.

decisions.label: Selection rule
decisions.value: sim2real's select() (cards/schema.py), mirrored rather than imported so the runtime stays numpy + stdlib: the lowest fit whose held-out rms ÷ noise floor ≤ 1.5 (REACHES_FLOOR). When none reaches it, chosen is None and the printout says to swap or fill another slot. Preferred over an information criterion because the floor is observable on the rig and the ratio is the number sim2real already reports.

decisions.label: Noise floor
decisions.value: noise_floor(log) is a module function: the pooled within-plateau std of tau, computed from the held-out log's own plateau ids (the same formula as the check, which gives identical ratios: 20.28/1.00 and 1.03/1.57).

decisions.label: BIC removed
decisions.value: Bound.bic and the BIC-based Comparison are gone. A BIC on the fit log is the training-data choice the amendment rules out, and keeping it beside the new rule would have offered two choosers.

keepParts: The held-out Comparison table: each row is one slot swap ('friction: coulomb_viscous → stribeck') showing fit rms, held-out rms and ÷ floor, plus a closing line naming the rule. It splices onto any variant that can say what changed between two rungs.

The leakage guard: a fitted result remembers its training samples, and compare(..., on=) refuses a held-out log that shares any of them. That is 3 lines, and it makes 'choose on training data' an error rather than a silent mistake.

variants.name: Estimators that climb
variants.thesis: A Model is a scikit-learn-style estimator for one rung (from_datasheet, fit, predict, rms, score, get_params). A Family is model selection over its ladder: climb(datasheet, fit, test) fits each child rung on the fit plateaus, judges it on the held-out ones, and climbs only while the current rung is above 1.5x the rig's noise floor and a child beats it on held-out data.
variants.bestWhen: The question is 'which rung does this unit's data justify, and with which numbers'. You have a rig log split into fit and held-out plateaus, and you want a defensible pick explained by a table of held-out rms against the rig's own noise floor, plus SI values ready for MuJoCo/sim2real. The 'what now' flow is three calls: from_datasheet, fit, climb.
variants.losesWhen:
- **Browsing or authoring the type.** Parameters are a dict, so type checkers see no fields.
- **Logs without repeated conditions.** The floor needs plateau ids; a free trajectory would need a floor passed in.
- **Siblings that need different experiments.** LuGre needs dt and M3.load needs tau_load, so one plateau log mostly prints 'skipped'.
- **Terms the plateaus never excite.** The climb then picks the lower rung, which is right for the data and wrong for the servo.
- **A rung that pays only as part of a pair.** The greedy climb can miss it.
- **Two copies of the 1.5 limit.** The selection rule is restated from sim2real, so it now lives in two repos.

decisions.label: Lowest rung wins at the floor
decisions.value: Once the current rung reaches the floor, the climb stops even if a child scores lower held-out. Short of the floor, it climbs only to a child that beats the current rung held-out (Zach: if it doesn't improve test time performance, you are overfitting). Undo: drop the `reached` test in Family.climb.

decisions.label: Noise floor belongs to the log
decisions.value: noise_floor(test) is a module function: the pooled within-plateau std, framed as the held-out rms of the one estimator no rung can beat (each plateau's own mean). The climb computes 0.00417 / 0.00422 N·m; the check's own oracle prints 0.0042 for both.

decisions.label: One-rung lookahead in the table
decisions.value: The climb fits the children of the rung it stops at, so the table shows why it stopped (servo B: M3 1.57 next to M2 1.03). A rung no log can feed is listed with the reason it was skipped.

keepParts: Family.climb + Climb table: a greedy, tree-shaped version of sim2real's select(), judged on held-out data. Each row shows fit rms, held-out rms and ÷ floor, plus a verdict, and lists skipped rungs with their reason. It drops onto any variant's Family or Type kit.
noise_floor(log) framed as an estimator: the held-out rms of the 'knows every plateau mean' model, about 8 numpy lines with bincount. It is the yardstick the rule divides by.

variants.thesis: The Type is the entry point. It hands you a kit with its Models (the ladder), its Datasheet class, the rig Experiments that identify each Model, and its fidelity metric plus the rig's floor. So "datasheet + rig log, what now?" is servo.identify(fit, datasheet=ds), which returns every model those two cover and names the motion still missing. variants.bestWhen: The question is "what do I run next, and when do I stop climbing?" A new part arrives, and the kit says which models the datasheet already gives, which rig motion unlocks which rung, and which rung is good enough, judged on held-out plateaus against the rig's own floor. The rule and the floor live in one place per type, so every caller (scenario, sim2real cards, robotparts) chooses the same way. That place matches how sim2real already organizes kits per type.
variants.losesWhen: You want the Model alone, or your own selection rule. Model parameters are a values mapping, not typed fields, so type checkers see nothing. A hand-built Model outside a kit is awkward because identified_by points at the kit's Experiment objects. The choice rule belongs to the kit, so a caller who wants AIC, a margin or another split has to go around compare: it takes the held-out log, never the rule. The rule restates sim2real's select() and its 1.5 limit, so two repos hold copies until one imports the other. A type with no rung folders gets no experiments and no fidelity metric.

decisions.label: Where the held-out comparison lives
decisions.value: In the Kit, next to the fidelity metric and the floor it divides by: Kit.compare(found, held_out). The type owns the metric, so it owns the choice, and every caller chooses the same way. The Model stays a declaration with values; it gets no score method.

decisions.label: Selection rule
decisions.value: sim2real's cards.schema.select(): the lowest rung whose held-out RMS ÷ the rig's pooled within-plateau std is at most TWINNED_LIMIT = 1.5. Same-level siblings are ranked by ratio, and chosen is None when no rung reaches the limit (the table then says to climb). No information criterion: the type already has a physical yardstick, the rig's repeatability.

decisions.label: compare refuses the fit log
decisions.value: Identified keeps the log it was fitted on (.log). compare raises ValueError when the held-out log shares a plateau with it. Choosing on training data is impossible, not merely discouraged. A plain dict of models, with no .log, still compares.

decisions.label: Training ratio shown, never chosen on
decisions.value: Comparison.on_fit puts the fit-plateau ratio beside the held-out ratio, so case B shows the overfit itself: M3 0.99 on fit and 1.57 held out, against M2 1.01 and 1.03.

keepParts: Kit.compare(found, held_out) with the refusal guard: Identified remembers its fit log, and comparing on overlapping plateaus raises. This makes 'choose on test, not train' a property of the API, and it splices onto any variant whose fit returns an object.
The comparison table with a 'fit x floor' column beside 'held-out rms / floor / x floor / twinned', which shows overfitting on its own (case B: M3 0.99 on fit, 1.57 held out).
Identified.missing plus Experiment ids derived from robotparts' measured_by: 'M3.lugre: run small_reversals' is the 'what now' answer when no rung reaches the floor.
proof: Simulated: The rig logs are the fixture's simulation, read through rig_log(case, "fit"|"test"); _truth.py is never read. Only velocity-plateau logs are read (velocity_plateaus, slow_plateaus). Chirps, reversals, pendulum sweeps and board calibration are named as Experiments, but their logs are not read. COVERAGE accepts 5 plateau speeds held both ways, not robotparts' 6-8, because the fit half of the alternating split holds 5; judging coverage on the whole run is left out. Physics runs for M0-M3 only: M3.load needs a tau_load input, M3.lugre runs at steady state, M3.weakening_capture is structure only, and M4-M7 are declared and raise on predict. The fitter is separable least squares (lstsq on levels and slopes, a scan plus golden-section search on one speed scale), numpy only; optional terms such as stribeck_exponent are defaulted, never fitted. The selection rule is a local copy of sim2real's select() and 1.5 limit, not an import. The module is type_kit.py, not robot_models.types, so it does not shadow the stdlib types module. Building every kit at import takes about 0.4 s.

media.label: Adding a rung
media.caption: What a contributor writes to add a new M3 friction model.
media.html: Two steps, both as today. (1) Add Rung(level=3, name=..., base=..., adds=..., code="actuators/rungs/<word>", equation=..., references=...) to actuators/servo/ladder.py. (2) Add the folder actuators/rungs/<word>/ with model.py (torque(terms, inputs, state, dt)) and model.json, with a measured_by on each term, in robotparts' format. With no registration, the kit then gives it a card, a place on the tree, Experiments (a new motion text becomes a new Experiment), predict, identify once a log covers its motions, and a row in compare's held-out choice. One more line is needed only when the rung names a new motion that identify should read from a log (a COVERAGE entry). A new fitter is needed only when the rung is not linear in levels and slopes plus one speed scale.

media.label: Migration from v1
media.caption: What changes for the ruler, robotparts' vendoring and sim2real's parity test.
media.html: Additive; nothing in v1 moves. (1) v1 ruler tests/test_ladders_acceptance.py: unchanged. Kit wraps Ladder (kit.ladder), so rung keys, bases, parameters(), aliases and packed names stay v1's. Landing it means adding src/robot_models/types.py plus two tests: every measured_by motion in a rung's model.json has a COVERAGE entry or is declared unreadable, and compare chooses on held-out plateaus (case A to M3.stribeck, case B to M2) and raises on the fit log. (2) robotparts vendoring of actuators/rungs/*: unchanged. The kit reads model.json and model.py read-only and exec's the rung source rather than importing it, so it leaves no __pycache__ and robotparts' byte-for-byte sha256 sync holds. (3) sim2real tests/test_robot_models_parity.py: unchanged; it reads ladders(), which stays. New coupling: Kit.compare restates sim2real's select() and TWINNED_LIMIT = 1.5, so landing should either share one constant (a parity assertion that both equal 1.5) or move select() into robot_models for sim2real to call. Later, sim2real's CameraKit and this Kit can converge on one shape. Rig logs passed to identify and compare need a plateau id per sample, or exact speed repeats as the fallback.
